newsitem.title: USA: LCI Int'l drops sharply on softer revs forecast.
newsitem.headline: LCI Int'l drops sharply on softer revs forecast.

text.p: Shares of LCI International Inc dropped sharply after the long distance company told analysts its future revenue growth will be below its earlier estimates.
LCI's shares fell 4-3/8 to 21-1/8 and topped the New York Stock Exchange's most actives list.
LCI told analysts it expects to see future revenue growth of about 30 percent, which is below its previous estimate for up to 40 percent growth, said Jim Hern, an analyst with Olde Discount Corp.

LCI also told analysts it expects to post fourth quarter revenues of about $292-$294 million. The company said its fourth quarter earnings may be about $0.01 a share below Wall Street estimates of $0.24-$0.25 a share, analysts said.
LCI could not be immediately reached for comment.

On Wednesday, LCI said it expects to report revenue and earnings growth for the fourth quarter. The company did not provide a specific forecast but said its fourth quarter results will reflect five to six percent growth in minutes.
Analysts said LCI's stock is suffering the same fate as that of telecommunications company Frontier Corp, which dropped sharply on Tuesday.
Frontier fell after it said its fourth quarter earnings would be below analysts' estimates and year-ago results.
"LCI is down on fears that the same factors that are hurting Frontier would hurt LCI too," Hern said.
"There's some concern about long-distance companies right now since some major customers like Excel (Communications Inc) said they would migrate their business away from Frontier," Hern said.
LCI's fourth quarter results are often weaker due to reduced corporate calling during the holidays. But the first quarter should show some improvement, analysts said.
LCI had been restricted until this week from talking publicly about its results, due to a quiet period related to an earlier acquisition.
The quiet period ender after some shareholders withdrew their request for a secondary offering of 1.45 million shares due to recent poor performance of long distance company stocks.
PaineWebber Thursday raised its rating on LCI to buy from attractive. Additional details were not immediately available.
Shares of telecommunications company MFS Communications Co Inc also dropped 2-1/4 to 46-1/4.
